- When sentiment is high (≥0.6), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for 2–3 periods.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30d horizon; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 0.4→0.7→0.9), model tends to lag; adjust forecast up by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment drops sharply (e.g., 0.8→0.1), model often fails to correct; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid underreaction.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias in 30d horizon; if 30d forecast is >10% above recent 10d average, reduce by 1–2%.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 periods.
